events.msg: Core toolkit: flagged transaction, card window, card baseline, recurring charges, resolved account history, device neighbours, region activity and prior cases

hypotheses: Friendly fraud or customer forgetfulness: The transaction is legitimate, as the generic device profile was used 9 times previously on this card and the amount is highly typical.
Card-Not-Present fraud or Account Takeover: An unauthorized party obtained the card details, though the generic device signature makes it difficult to distinguish from the customer's own browser.
Unrecognized recurring subscription: The transaction is a recurring charge that the customer does not recognize or forgot they signed up for.

calls.why: To examine the full transaction history on this card, looking for patterns of usage, previous successful transactions, and whether the generic device profile has a long history of legitimate use.
To check if there are prior transactions of a similar amount ($55.68) on this card, which would point to a recurring subscription or billing agreement.

events.msg: Four specialist analysts reviewing their evidence in parallel

events.assessment: The flagged transaction 3558054 is highly suspicious and likely fraudulent, as confirmed by the customer's direct dispute. The card has experienced a high volume of transactions within a 72-hour window using multiple different email domains (gmail.com, hotmail.es, hotmail.com, outlook.com) and various device profiles, indicating a compromised card being used across different platforms.
key_points: The customer C13171 explicitly disputed transaction 3558054 ($55.68), which has a high transaction model score of 0.599057.

The 72-hour window shows a rapid succession of transactions with shifting email addresses, such as gmail.com (e.g., 3553281), hotmail.es (3553275), and outlook.com (3554589), which is highly anomalous for a single cardholder.
Multiple distinct device profiles were used in a short period, including mobile devices like SM-G900M (3553223) and Huawei ALE-L23 (3550100), alongside generic desktop signatures.

events.assessment: The customer C13171 has reported transaction 3558054 ($55.68) as unauthorized. The account history shows three prior transactions on the same day (2016-12-19) using generic mobile and desktop browser signatures, with low risk scores from the transaction model. Because the flagged device profile is a generic browser signature, we cannot definitively link it to a specific device or fraud ring.
key_points: Customer C13171 reported transaction 3558054 as unauthorized, which is the fourth transaction on card C13171-K2.
The account history shows three prior transactions (3555768, 3556719, and 3557118) occurring within a 16-hour window on 2016-12-19.
The flagged device profile ' |  | chrome 66.0 | ' is a generic browser signature and does not provide strong evidence of a specific fraud ring or account takeover on its own.

events.assessment: The transaction 3558054 reported by customer C13171 is an isolated claim of unauthorized use. Although the device profile is shared with 175 other cards across numerous transactions, this high volume indicates a generic browser signature rather than a coordinated fraud ring or account takeover.
key_points: Customer C13171 reported transaction 3558054 ($55.68) as unauthorized.
The device profile associated with the transaction is shared with 175 other cards all-time, including cards C03218-K2, C10245-K1, and C08962-K2.
This extremely high number of associated cards indicates a generic browser signature shared by many unrelated users, which is not evidence of a fraud ring.

events.assessment: The customer C13171 has reported an unrecognized transaction of $55.68 (ID 3558054) on card C13171-K2. This customer has an extensive history of confirmed fraud cases on this same card identifier, consistently involving unauthorized card-not-present transactions from new devices. Given this established pattern of recurring compromise, the current alert is highly likely to be another instance of card-not-present fraud.
key_points: Customer C13171 has at least eight prior closed fraud cases (including CC-2716, CC-0467, CC-2059, CC-4485, CC-4163, CC-2244, CC-2454, and CC-0772) all associated with card C13171-K2.
Prior cases were confirmed as fraud, involving unauthorized online purchases from various new devices (such as Windows, Android, and Moto G devices) inconsistent with the cardholder's history.
Despite repeated actions to block and reissue, the card identifier C13171-K2 remains associated with ongoing fraudulent activity.

events.claim: The transaction model trained on the bank's own closed cases (4,665 confirmed-fraud and 900 cleared investigations, July-October; October hold-out AUC 0.973) scores this transaction 0.599, against a 2.1% base rate. It reads the unnamed Vesta C/D/M/V columns, the identity record, running aggregates of the resolved account and the graph's memory of earlier closed cases, all as known at transaction time (it never sees the case outcome)
